title: Non-pressure ulcer depth and burn extent
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the ulcer, or for the burn extent (T31) when the note is about a burn (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Scald burns

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F
Recent Labs: WBC 8.4 x 10^9/L, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Hematocrit 37%, Sodium 139 mEq/L, Potassium 4.0 mEq/L, Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, eGFR 82 mL/min/1.73m2.

Social History: Retired teacher, lives with her spouse. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol consumption.
Family History: Mother had hypertension; father had a myocardial infarction at age 65.
Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or fatigue.
Integumentary: Positive for localized pain, erythema, and blistering.
Neurological: Negative for dizziness or confusion.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath or cough.

History of Present Illness:
Patient is a 72-year-old female who presented to the emergency department after sustaining scald burns while cooking in her kitchen. The patient reports that boiling water spilled onto her torso and upper extremities. She was evaluated for acute thermal injury and admitted for specialized wound management and fluid resuscitation.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for the management of scald burns covering 15% of the body surface area. Clinical examination revealed that of the total area involved, 5% are third degree (full thickness) injuries located on the anterior torso. The patient was started on aggressive fluid resuscitation and transitioned to a specialized burn dressing regimen. Wound care was performed daily to maintain sterility and promote healing of the full thickness areas. The patient tolerated the treatment well, with no signs of infection. Pain was managed with scheduled analgesics. She was transitioned to oral medications for pain and transitioned to a plan for outpatient dressing care.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Scald burns (15% total body surface area)
- Third-degree burns (5% total body surface area)

Discharge Medications:
- Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Bacitracin ointment to be applied to dressings twice daily

Follow-up:
Follow up with the outpatient burn clinic in 7 days for wound assessment and dressing change.

Electronically signed, A. Rivera, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Burns of 10-19% of the body with under 10% third degree: T31.10 (no HCC).
